clue.text: Fellow of Somerville long confined — such poor health

indicators.note: being confined means being shut inside, so one piece sits within the other here

parts.note: Edith Somerville wrote with her cousin under the pen name Martin Ross: the Irish literary duo Somerville and Ross
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: An Oxford don at the women's college Somerville, bedridden for ages with wretched health.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerville looks like the Oxford women's college, but it is Edith Somerville, who wrote Irish novels with her cousin as the pair Somerville and Ross; 'confined' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropy is informal British for unwell or below par, so this noun is the state of feeling poorly.

clue.text: Pop singer makes a good swimmer

parts.note: rock is popular music
a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice

explanation.surface: A pop star turns out to be strong in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock bass is a North American freshwater fish of the sunfish family.

clue.text: The legs and stomach you'd expect to see on City gent

definitions.text: you'd expect to see on City gent

parts.note: pins is slang for the legs
tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as food

explanation.surface: A bowler-hatted financier with his skinny legs and paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose businessmen traditionally wear pinstriped suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe suit, cloth with thin pale lines, was the uniform of London bankers.

clue.text: Just the place up in Cheshire, though not county

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the short word is read from bottom to top
though not means a piece is taken away from the word before

parts.note: a shire is a county

explanation.surface: The perfect spot, up in Cheshire, though not out in the county itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IN into NI; 'though not' removes SHIRE (county) from Cheshire, an English county, leaving CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a position exactly suited to someone, the ideal slot.

clue.text: George, a child who's proverbially happy…

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
a boy is a male child

explanation.surface: George, a youngster famous for his cheerfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: George is the novelist George Sand; 'happy as a sandboy' is a British saying for someone carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying happy as a sandboy describes a person utterly content.

clue.text: Got through history oral

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for history is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: history is the past

explanation.surface: Someone passed their oral history exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral' makes PAST, a word for history, into its spoken twin PASSED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have passed a test or a stage is to have got through it successfully.

clue.text: he has an American car good auction purchase

parts.note: auto is American for a car
pi, short for pious, means good
a lot is an item bought at auction

explanation.surface: Continuing from George: he owns a US car, a bargain bought at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 4 Down: 'he' is George, airmen's slang for an aircraft's automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George was the RAF nickname for the automatic flight-control system, so 'he' is that device.

clue.text: How, structuralism starts to destroy art

indicators.note: starts means just the opening letter of structuralism is taken

parts.note: to kill is to destroy

explanation.surface: How the theory of structuralism begins to wreck the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes S from structuralism.
explanation.definitionFit: Art in the older sense is a craft or skill, as in the art of cooking.

clue.text: Big mammal savages gun-dog

indicators.note: savages means attacks violently, so the letters are mauled into a new shape

explanation.surface: A large beast attacks a retriever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savages' rearranges GUNDOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a large plant-eating sea mammal of the Indian Ocean, a relative of the manatee.

clue.text: Somewhat delicate and beautiful, and possessing money

indicators.note: possessing means holding something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: fairy is used as an adjective for something dainty and lovely
L is the pound sign, standing for money

explanation.surface: A rather dainty, pretty person who is also well off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessing' puts L, the pound (from Latin libra), inside FAIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly means moderately or to some degree.

clue.text: Not saying much in the absence of the French section

indicators.note: in the absence of tells us one piece goes missing from the longer word

parts.note: laconic means using very few words
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A taciturn section of a meeting, quiet now the French delegation has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the absence of' removes LA (French 'the') from LACONIC; 'section' as the definition stands for a conic section, the curve made by slicing a cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A conic is short for a conic section, a curve such as an ellipse cut from a cone by a plane.

clue.text: Turning up missing the start is almost a disaster

indicators.note: missing the start means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: turning up something buried is unearthing it

explanation.surface: Turning up without the opening moments nearly turned into a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the start' takes the first letter U off UNEARTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, a mishap only just avoided.

clue.text: Goat has difficulty coming back to plant

parts.note: a goat butts, so it is jocularly a butter

indicators.note: coming back means this word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: rub means a difficulty, as in there's the rub

explanation.surface: A goat struggles to return to the plant it was grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: The goat is jocularly 'one that butts'; 'coming back' reverses the word for difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterbur is a broad-leaved wild flower of damp ground, related to the daisy.

clue.text: In speech, exaggerate support for power

indicators.note: in speech tells us the phrase is to be heard spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: to pile it on is to exaggerate

explanation.surface: A speaker overstating the case for electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In speech' turns PILE ON (exaggerate) into the like-sounding PYLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is the steel tower holding up overhead electricity cables.

clue.text: Track where Titanic went down originally

definitions.text: Track where Titanic went down originally

parts.words: Track where Titanic went down originally
parts.note: not the Atlantic seabed: the first descent of any new ship is down the sloping launch ramp at the shipyard

explanation.surface: Retracing the route of the doomed liner to where it first sank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went down' suggests the sinking of 1912, but the ship first went down the ramp into the water at its launch in Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is the inclined ramp down which a newly built vessel slides into the water.

clue.text: Alert runners in Yorkshire

parts.note: to wake is to rouse or alert
the field is all the runners in a race

explanation.surface: Warning the competitors in a Yorkshire race.
explanation.walkthrough: The field means all the horses or athletes taking part in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakefield is a cathedral city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Cry out in pain, having no courage

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelling in pain because they are a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, lacking nerve.

clue.text: Prepared to inflame with envy? O dear, how unfortunate

indicators.note: how unfortunate suggests things gone awry, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone poised to stir up jealousy, and alas, how regrettable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how unfortunate' rearranges ENVY and O DEAR; 'inflame' looks emotional but means set in the heat of an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-ready food is prepared in advance and needs only cooking in the heat.

clue.text: Tired? Run like crazy from possible burglar

indicators.note: like crazy suggests wild disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exhausted burglar suspect still running for dear life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like crazy' rearranges TIRED and RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder enters premises uninvited, as a housebreaker does.

clue.text: Almost tugging at jacket

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: jerking is tugging sharply

explanation.surface: Someone nearly pulling at a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter G from JERKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless close-fitting short coat.

clue.text: The French resort to touchy extremes of delicacy

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of touchy

explanation.surface: The French go to sensitive lengths in matters of tact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a verb after 'The French' but is the noun: Nice; 'extremes of' takes the first and last letters of touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine distinction or subtle detail, a matter of precision.

clue.text: Salesman's spiel to accompany new model

parts.note: patter is the glib talk of a salesman

explanation.surface: A sales pitch that goes with the launch of the latest model.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template to be copied.

clue.text: Speed up in part of book identifying Rabelais' rascal

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a page is part of a book

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for speed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to run is to speed

explanation.surface: Racing through a section of Rabelais to find his rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RUN into NUR, which goes 'in' PAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Panurge is the roguish companion of Pantagruel in Rabelais' comic novels.

clue.text: Out of control in a snow hazard

parts.note: a drift is a bank of snow piled by wind

explanation.surface: A driver losing control in deep snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat adrift floats free with nobody steering, so it is directionless.

clue.text: Star in stunt

definitions.meaning: a ... is a small dim star, as in white ...
to stunt growth is to keep something small

explanation.surface: A celebrity performing a dangerous trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on smallness: a little faint star, and the verb meaning to keep something undersized.

clue.text: Aboard Britannia, I slept in the gangway

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so the answer is carried inside these words

explanation.surface: On the royal yacht Britannia, a passenger dozed in the passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Britannia was the British royal yacht, which makes 'Aboard' fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats.

clue.text: Woman who stooped to win gold

parts.note: to conquer is to win
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A woman who lowered herself to take the gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Goldsmith's comedy She Stoops to Conquer, whose heroine stoops to conquer and so is a winner of hearts; 'win' doubles in sense only on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith's heroine in She Stoops to Conquer lowers herself to win her man, making her a victor.

clue.text: He taught the man who dated Creation, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the name is to be heard spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: Archbishop James Ussher dated the Creation to 4004 BC

explanation.surface: A teacher once taught the scholar who fixed the date of Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns the name of Archbishop Ussher, who dated the Creation to 4004 BC, into the like-sounding word for an old school assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher was formerly an assistant schoolmaster, an under-teacher.

clue.text: Dramatically, one calls a policeman

definitions.meaning: J B Priestley's play is titled An ... Calls, with 'one' standing for 'an'
a police officer of rank above sergeant

explanation.surface: In a theatrical moment, someone phones for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatically' points to the stage: An Inspector Calls is J B Priestley's play, with 'one' standing for 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's visitor is a detective of that rank, and in British police forces the rank sits above sergeant.

clue.text: Tried to get right inside the subject

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a head is a subject heading, a topic

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to get to the heart of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts R into HEAD, a subject or heading; 'Tried' is the court sense, a case that has been heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that has been tried in court has been heard by the judge.

clue.text: Originally thin and weak, but hearty about the outdoor life

indicators.note: originally means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: weedy means feeble or puny

explanation.surface: Someone once skinny and feeble who now loves the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweedy suggests the hearty country type in tweeds, fond of hunting and walking.

clue.text: Judas tree and bay entwined by river

indicators.note: entwined means twisted together, so these letters are woven into a new order

explanation.surface: A Judas tree and a bay tree grow tangled together beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entwined' rearranges TREE and BAY into BETRAYE, then R (river) ends it; Judas the tree is a decoy for Judas the disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot handed Jesus over to his enemies, so his name means a traitor.
